<b>I — обонятельный нерв.</b> Около 20 п: I — olfactory nerve. About 20 fiber bundles (the olfactory filaments) rise from the nasal cavity through the ethmoid bone into the olfactory bulb. It enters the telencephalon directly: the only route into the cortex that bypasses the thalamus.
<b>XI — добавочный нерв</b> обособляется: XI — the accessory nerve becomes a separate nerve in amniotes (reptiles, birds, mammals). It is purely motor; some of its roots come from the spinal cord. It works with the muscles of the shoulder girdle and neck: it turns the head.
\n <div><h2>Как их запомнить</h2>\n:
How to remember them

Sensory: I, II, VIII: smell, vision, the inner ear (hearing and balance). Motor: IV, VI, XI, XII. Motor with parasympathetic fibers: III (constricts the pupil). Mixed: V, VII, IX, X: in their set of functions they are closest to spinal nerves; parasympathetic fibers also run in VII, IX and X.

Where they emerge

I enters the telencephalon, II the diencephalon. III and IV emerge from the midbrain (IV is the only one on the dorsal side). V is associated with the pons. VI, VII and VIII emerge at the border of the pons and the medulla, IX–XII from the medulla.

Evolution

The set did not appear all at once: fish and amphibians have no separate XI and XII nerves (their fibers run within the vagus and spinal nerves), and the full set of 12 pairs is found in amniotes: reptiles, birds and mammals. The medulla and pons retain the plan of the spinal cord: sensory nuclei lie laterally, motor nuclei medially, and parasympathetic nuclei between them.

What is accurate here

  • Where the nerves emerge on the underside of the brain.
  • Classification by function and the direction of the signal.
  • The ganglion and three branches of the trigeminal nerve.

<b>Инфекции, передающиеся половым путём: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Many of them run without symptoms for a long time, so a person may not know they are infected and may pass the infection on. Protection: condoms, vaccines (HPV, hepatitis B), regular testing and treatment of both partners, HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis. Pathogens are not to scale: bacteria are 5–10 times larger than viruses. Click a pathogen.
<b>Фолиевая кислота</b> (лат. folium — л: Folic acid (Latin folium — leaf). Its reduced form, tetrahydrofolate, carries one-carbon groups for the synthesis of purines and thymidine — without it DNA cannot be replicated. Deficiency: megaloblastic anemia, and in the fetus, neural tube defects, so it is prescribed when planning a pregnancy. Methotrexate (the “Active form” button) is its structural analog, an anticancer drug. Sources: leafy greens, liver, legumes.
<b>Витамин D3 (холекальциферол)</b> обра: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is formed in the skin under ultraviolet light from a cholesterol derivative. The liver adds OH at position 25 and the kidneys at position 1, giving the hormone calcitriol (the “Active form” button), which increases intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate. Deficiency: rickets in children, osteomalacia in adults. Sources: sunlight, oily fish, eggs.
<b>Витамин K</b> нужен ферменту, который: Vitamin K is needed by the enzyme that converts glutamate residues into γ-carboxyglutamate in clotting factors II, VII, IX and X: only then can they bind calcium and work. Deficiency causes bleeding; newborns are given vitamin K. Warfarin (the “Active form” button) is a vitamin K antagonist, a drug against blood clots. Sources: green leaves (K1), gut bacteria (K2).
20 amino acids are the alphabet of proteins. All of them share a common part (an amino group, a carboxyl group and a hydrogen atom on the α-carbon) and differ in their side chain. They are grouped by the properties of the side chain (ring color). All protein amino acids except glycine are L-isomers. The nine essential amino acids (valine, leucine, isoleucine, threonine, methionine, lysine, phenylalanine, tryptophan and histidine) cannot be made by humans and must come from food; children also need arginine. \n <div><h2>Белки</h2>\n <p>:
Proteins

Proteins are polymers of L-α-amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Functions: enzymes, transport (hemoglobin, albumin), defense (antibodies), movement (actin, myosin), structure (collagen, keratin), regulation (protein hormones), receptors.

Properties

Proteins are amphoteric polyelectrolytes; at the isoelectric point their net charge is zero and their solubility is minimal. They are precipitated by salting out (reversibly) and by heavy-metal salts (irreversibly), and separated by electrophoresis and chromatography.

Folding diseases

Misfolded proteins clump together into amyloid: Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases, prion diseases (Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease).

  • Hemoglobin — PDB 4HHB, chaperonin — 1AON, lysozyme — 1AKI. Chaperonin and lysozyme are shown at the same scale; while the protein is inside, the front half of the chaperonin is cut away so that the cavity under the GroES lid is visible.
  • The unfolded chain is a random coil with the same residues; the transition between the coil and the native form is a smooth interpolation, not a real folding pathway.
  • Amino acids are built from their formulas, without hydrogen atoms.

\n <div><h2>Нуклеиновые кислоты</h2:
Nucleic acids

DNA is a polymer of deoxyribonucleotides (A, G, C, T) that stores hereditary information in the nucleus and mitochondria. RNA is made of ribonucleotides (A, G, C, U) and is usually single-stranded: mRNA, tRNA, rRNA and regulatory RNAs.

Replication enzymes

  • Helicase, topoisomerases (the target of quinolones and some anticancer drugs), SSB.
  • Primase — RNA primers.
  • DNA polymerases (α, δ, ε in humans) — synthesis and 3′→5′ proofreading.
  • DNA ligase. At chromosome ends — telomerase.

Mutations

Point mutations (substitution, insertion or deletion of a nucleotide), frameshift mutations, chromosomal mutations. Mutagens: UV and ionizing radiation, chemicals, viruses. Repair systems: direct repair, excision repair (base and nucleotide excision) and mismatch repair.

Models

  • DNA dodecamer — PDB 1BNA, all heavy atoms; hydrogen bonds are found from the distances between the nitrogen and oxygen atoms of the bases.
  • The strands differ in the color of the backbone tube and of the carbon atoms (light blue and orange); the grooves are labeled where they face the viewer.

\n <div><h2>Гемоглобин</h2>\n:
Hemoglobin

A chromoprotein: the protein globin + 4 hemes. Normal range: 130–160 g/L in men, 120–140 g/L in women. Forms: HbA (α₂β₂, 97%), HbA₂ (α₂δ₂), fetal HbF (α₂γ₂). Derivatives: oxyhemoglobin, deoxyhemoglobin, carbaminohemoglobin (CO₂ on amino groups), carboxyhemoglobin (CO), methemoglobin (Fe³⁺), glycated HbA1c (reflects average blood sugar over 2–3 months in diabetes).

CO₂ transport

About 10% of CO₂ is carried in the blood as carbaminohemoglobin, the rest as bicarbonate: red cell carbonic anhydrase converts CO₂ + H₂O into H₂CO₃ → H⁺ + HCO₃⁻; the H⁺ is taken up by hemoglobin (a buffer).

Hemoglobinopathies

Qualitative (HbS and hundreds of other mutant hemoglobins) and quantitative — thalassemias (reduced synthesis of α or β chains).
